title: Technical sales, solutions and implementation

skills.name: Technical product explanation
skills.asked_for: Making a system understandable to a non-technical buyer
skills.evidence: Client-facing work at K2 Digital Media, explaining web, SEO and content work to small business owners.

skills.name: Client communication
skills.evidence: K2 Digital Media client management, plus a year of customer-facing work at Bill Gosling Outsourcing.

skills.name: Demo delivery
skills.asked_for: Running a live product walkthrough without losing the room
skills.evidence: Client presentations of his own work. Not structured product demos against a script.
skills.limit: Not structured product demos against a script.

skills.name: Requirements gathering
skills.asked_for: Turning a vague business ask into a scoped piece of work
skills.evidence: Standard agency practice at K2, every client engagement starts there.

skills.name: Technical breadth
skills.asked_for: Enough across web, cloud, integrations and data to hold a technical conversation
skills.evidence: Full stack, automation and support background gives unusually wide coverage for this lane.

skills.name: CRM usage
skills.asked_for: HubSpot, Salesforce or similar, pipeline hygiene
skills.evidence: Agency-level client tracking. Not an enterprise CRM in a sales process.
skills.limit: Not an enterprise CRM in a sales process.

skills.name: Implementation and onboarding
skills.evidence: Delivers client projects end to end at K2, which is the same shape at smaller scale.
skills.limit: Delivers client projects end to end at K2, which is the same shape at smaller scale.

positioning:
Running K2 Digital Media is the argument for this lane, and it is a genuinely good one: he sells, scopes, delivers and supports technical work for real clients under his own name. That is the entire job of a solutions or implementation seat at junior level. The gap is that he has done it as an owner rather than inside a sales organisation, so he has no experience of a pipeline, a quota, or a formal sales process.

Most in-scope postings here grade Tier A or Tier B. Keep this lane opportunistic: it is not a priority lane, it should never displace a priority-lane role, and the NOC trap means a careless row here does real damage by suggesting a PR pathway that is not there.
interview_watch: Expect "sell me this product" and expect a question about a time a customer was unhappy. The Bill Gosling year and the K2 client work both answer the second one well. Be ready for a direct question about whether he actually wants sales, since owning an agency reads as someone who may leave to run it full time. Have an honest answer.
pr_note: 62100 is on the Altona and Rhineland RCIP list, and AIP covers it from a designated Atlantic employer. Ontario's Workforce Priority stream takes it with a qualifying offer. The trap in this lane is the NOC, not the skill: non-technical sales is 64100 or 64101 and is not PR-eligible. Only genuinely technical seats map to 62100.
not_required: Quota-carrying sales experience. If a posting requires it, that posting is 64100 and out of scope.

notes.heading: Intro
notes.text: NOC 62100, TEER 2. Secondary lane, opportunistic. Read 00-index.md for the Status conventions and tier rules.

notes.heading: The gate before the matrix
notes.text: A role enters this lane only if the body shows real technical content: demos he would run, systems he would configure, integrations he would scope, or customers he would implement for. A posting carrying a hard sales quota is a sales seat. It maps to 64100, it is not PR-eligible, and it is dropped rather than graded. Read the compensation paragraph: on-target earnings and commission structure without technical duties is the tell.
